correctness.rationale: Generalized Hall proves each common EQ level via a capacity-t incidence matching; every leftover good has a nonapprover (n>=3, support<=2). The identity |N(S)|=D|S|-e(S) yields t*=D-pseudoarboricity>=floor(D/2), which forces EF1 because cross-bundle value is at most D-t*<=t*+1. Counting pair goods gives m=nD-e(N); a set witnessing lambda>=1 contains at least 2lambda-1 pair goods; two vertices with 2lambda-1 parallel shared goods attain the bound. Monotonicity yields the all-profile sharp maximum. A self-contained checker passed 346 normalized sparse multiplicity configurations and 51 independently brute-forced exhaustive allocations; these finite checks do not replace the proof.

value.rationale: The result establishes an all-agent-count non-laminar structured domain for exact EQ simultaneously with EF1 and gives the sharp utilitarian price at every natural pseudoarboricity density level. It is motivated by the known difficulty of joint envy/equity and distinguishes graph congestion from merely item count. A polynomial-time constructive proof and extremal two-agent overlap witnesses give a meaningful structural classification; unlike arbitrary small instances it is uniform in n and D. Wastefulness and inaccessible-primary-source risks are stated.
